minutes.headline: Select Board recommended most routine warrant articles, deferred money-less ones, and sent appointment process back for another week.
minutes.summary: The board heard sponsors of several annual town meeting articles, including an agricultural preservation restriction, a Salary Administration Plan amendment, zoning changes and a cemetery transfer. It voted to convey land to the Conservation Commission and ratified a van driver, then spent a long, divided stretch on the reappointment procedure without resolving it. Near the end it voted recommendations on articles with known amounts and held off on those lacking numbers.

budget_items.topic: Agricultural preservation restriction, Pierce's Christmas tree farm
budget_items.what_was_said: Article asks for the 10 percent local match with the state paying the rest; the APR is valued at the stated amount.
State normally asks a 20 percent municipal match but reduced it to 10 because the town has an agricultural commission and right to farm bylaw.
A board member noted the reduced match saved the town money versus the usual match.
Article transfers funds from the sale of cemetery lots for care and improvement, with annual expenses including website hosting.
The warrant closed with a set number of articles, two being citizen petitions.
Existing conditions plan update can be covered under the FY21 facilities budget, avoiding inclusion in the town meeting design article; landscape design funding to come from free cash.
The state earmark must be spent by June 30, 2021 unless the legislature extends it, and the project needs full funding in place.
Town deposit follows financial policy of 10 percent of prior year's certified free cash; sewer commission deposit is a consistent amount.
Small separate area billed for water bought from Fitchburg; usual operating amount stated.
Sending leftover borrowing, mainly from the high school feasibility study.

what_happened.line: The board spent a long, divided stretch on the appointment and reappointment procedure and closed it for the night without resolving it.
By consensus it moved step four of the appointment procedure to the first Friday in April and the application deadline to the second Thursday in May.
The board will not recommend articles that lack a stated sum, such as the budget, capital, transfers, solid waste and cable, until numbers are available.
It voted recommendations on routine articles, merged the two OPEB deposit articles into one, and deferred to town meeting on the off-street parking article.
The Salary Administration Plan article was referred to the personnel committee, which is to vote on removing the longevity pay piece before the 30th.

why_it_matters: Articles with no stated sum, including the budget, are not yet recommended, so residents will not see the board's position on them until it votes again, possibly on the 30th.
The agricultural preservation restriction and the OPEB and sewer reserve deposits are items on the warrant that residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
How volunteers on town boards are reappointed is still undecided, and any change would apply to residents who serve on commissions.
watch_next: March 30 meeting, when warrant articles are to be approved for printing and the board may take up articles that still lack numbers.
Personnel committee vote, due before the 30th, on removing the longevity pay piece from the Salary Administration Plan article.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main recommendation votes, the dollar figures and the March 30 meeting date, but our captions could not hear most vote outcomes, so those rest on the official minutes. The main differences are the OPEB article L/CC vote, which only we record; the Q and V article descriptions, which differ; and several board decisions (longevity pay, the stated-sum rule, the parking article) that only our recording has.
